neet_che_u07_t11_1.working: In the Leclanche cell, zinc is oxidised (Zn → Zn2+ + 2e-), so the zinc container is the anode. The graphite rod is the cathode.

neet_che_u07_t11_2.working: Mn is +4 in MnO2. In MnO(OH), Mn + (-2) + (-1) = 0 gives Mn = +3. So the change is +4 to +3.

neet_che_u07_t11_3.working: During discharge, Pb and PbO2 are both converted to PbSO4 and H2SO4 is consumed, so the acid density decreases. The PbO2 grid is the cathode, not the anode. Only option 2 is correct.

neet_che_u07_t11_4.working: Anode of the dry cell is the zinc container (III). Electrolyte of the lead accumulator is about 38% H2SO4 (IV). Cathode of the lead accumulator is the PbO2 grid (I). Electrolyte of the dry cell is the NH4Cl/ZnCl2 paste (II).

neet_che_u07_t11_5.working: A is true: the dry cell is a primary cell. B is true: NH3 complexes with Zn2+ to give [Zn(NH3)4]2+. C is false: each lead accumulator cell gives about 2 V. D is true: charging regenerates Pb and PbO2. E is false: acid density decreases on discharge. Correct set is A, B, D.
